title: The Congo Club and Big Nick
summary: The Congo Club in the Norwood Hotel, where he joined the house band and Big Nick encouraged him.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: The Congo Club was located in the Norwood(?) Hotel, 555 East Adams Boulevard. It was like... East Adams Street, yeah. It was like the place. Slim Jenkins was the owner, and downstairs in the Norwood(?) Hotel, they had this very fine club, and it was called the Congo Club. Now, the Congo Club... When the big acts left the theatre, they would come into the Congo Club and work the following week, see.

From the Paradise Theatre, yeah. And they had a great, great band in there, a really good band, like some of the top players in the band... He really had started out the club with Kelly Martin, a fine drummer, and he had guys like Howard McGhee and a lot of great players who were in that band. But by the time I got there Howard was gone, but we knew about each other. Big Nick told me one night, he says, "Look, man," he says...

...talking about Rudy Rutherford or Sonny Stitt, because they felt that they were a little more experienced. They both were four years older than I was. And so, he said, "But I like what you're doing." He says, "You come on in and don't pay anybody any attention; you just come in here and do your work," you know.

So I first came to rehearsal that day, and we were playing in a shell... That's the first time I had really played in a shell where it really killed the sound. Boy, I could barely hear myself. So some of the guys were looking around at me funny...! [LAUGHS]
